aat-kobor.desc: On 5 August 1971 a group of freedom fighters sheltering at Jagannathpur moved towards Bagowan and ran into a Pakistani ambush laid in a sugarcane field by troops from the Natudah camp. Eight of them were killed in a fight that lasted about two and a half hours, and villagers buried them in two graves, four to each. The site, named Aat Kobor after those eight graves, now has a memorial complex with a small Liberation War museum, an open-air stage and gardens. Mujibnagar, where the first government of Bangladesh took oath, is only about 6 km away.
blocks: How to get there
From Chuadanga town take a bus or CNG to Damurhuda and on towards Natudah and Jagannathpur, or visit on the way to Mujibnagar from Meherpur.
Good to know
Combine it with the Mujibnagar Memorial the same day. It is close to the border, so carry ID and stay on the main road.

glance: 230 km to Chuadanga by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
karpashdanga.desc: Karpashdanga on the Bhairab river in Damurhuda was a busy trading place from Mughal to British times. The ruined Nilkuthi on the riverbank once served the indigo trade; part of it is now a school. Kazi Nazrul Islam stayed in the village for a time, and a small Nazrul memorial room keeps items linked to his visit. The village is also home to a long-established Christian community and church.
blocks: How to get there
From Chuadanga, go by bus or auto to Damurhuda and on to Karpashdanga.
Good to know
Ask at the local high school about seeing the Nazrul memorabilia.

glance: 230 km to Chuadanga by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
gholdari-shahi-mosque.desc: The mosque stands about a kilometre south-east of Gholdari bazar in Ailhas union of Alamdanga upazila. Local people credit a saint named Khairul Basar Omaj with building it and say he is buried in the grounds; the inscription stone is almost worn away, so the claimed date of around a thousand years ago cannot be checked. What you can see is a small three-domed prayer hall of thin bricks with lime-surki mortar, small minarets on the corners and painted leaf and flower designs on the walls. Banglapedia lists it among Chuadanga's archaeological sites, and the old Gholdari indigo kuthi is in the same area.
blocks: How to get there
From Chuadanga town take a bus or CNG towards Alamdanga, get off for Gholdari bazar, then walk or take a van about 1 km.
Good to know
It is still used for prayer; go outside prayer times and dress modestly.

glance: 230 km to Chuadanga by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
chuadanga-bara-masjid.desc: The Bara Masjid is the best-known mosque in Chuadanga town, built in a traditional three-domed style. It is a focal point of the town, especially during Friday prayers and Eid. The surrounding streets are lively with shops and tea stalls. It makes a short stop on a walk through town.
blocks: How to get there
In central Chuadanga; any rickshaw can take you.
Good to know
Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.

glance: Approx. 60–150 BDT per kg in season
Barobazar fruit market by the Mathabhanga, Chuadanga town
chuadanga-mango.desc: Chuadanga is one of the major mango districts of the south-west. Himsagar ripens first, followed by Langra, Amrapali, Fazli and late Ashwina. In season the town's fruit market heaves with baskets and trucks. Eating a ripe Himsagar straight from an orchard is the summer reward.

glance: Winter gur haats around Chuadanga and Alamdanga
chuadanga-khejur-gur.desc: Chuadanga has a large number of date palms, and winter gur is a big local trade. Tappers collect sap at dawn and boil it in shallow pans in the fields, filling the air with a sweet, smoky smell. Gur is sold liquid in pots or set into patali. It is the base of the season's pitha and payesh.

glance: 230 km to Chuadanga by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
thakurpur-jame-mosque.desc: Thakurpur Jame Mosque, also known as Pirganj Jame Mosque, stands in Thakurpur village beside the Chuadanga–Jhenaidah road, about 2 km from town. Elders say a Sufi called Afu Shah came from West Bengal in 1698 and set up a khanqah here, and that he raised the mosque in a single night with the help of jinn, hence the name Jiner Masjid. The grounds cover about 30 bighas, with a large pond behind the mosque, rows of coconut trees and a graveyard. The entrance and interior have been tiled, but the old inner part has been kept, and an urs is held every year on 12 Falgun.
blocks: How to get there
Take an easy-bike or rickshaw from Chuadanga town along the Jhenaidah road to Thakurpur (about 2 km).
Good to know
The annual urs on 12 Falgun (late February) draws big crowds. Dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

glance: 230 km to Chuadanga by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
darshana.desc: Darshana sits beside the Indian border on the old Kolkata rail line. Its sugar mill and distillery are run by Carew & Co, a company dating back to the colonial era and one of the oldest industrial names in the country. In the crushing season, trucks and bullock carts of sugarcane queue at the gates. The station and border crossing add to the town's busy, frontier feel.
blocks: How to get there
Train or bus from Chuadanga town (about 30–40 min).
Good to know
Industrial areas need permission to enter; view from outside unless you have arranged a visit.

chuadanga-indigo-heritage.desc: In the 19th century, British planters forced farmers in this region to grow indigo, leading to the Indigo Revolt of 1859–60. The planters' nilkuthis, or factory houses, still stand in ruins in Chuadanga and neighbouring Meherpur. Local memory of the period lives on in stories and place names. Visiting a nilkuthi gives context to this chapter of rural resistance.
blocks: Good to know
Combine Karpashdanga with Meherpur's Amjhupi Nilkuthi for a heritage day.

mathabhanga-riverfront.desc: The Mathabhanga flows past Chuadanga town and shapes its daily life. Along its banks you see fishermen casting nets, people bathing at ghats and boats crossing to villages. Near the river, the Barobazar fruit market is the hub of the mango trade in season. Evening walks here are a local habit.
blocks: How to get there
Walk or rickshaw from the town centre.
Good to know
Visit the fruit market early on a summer morning to see mango trading at its peak.

glance: 230 km to Chuadanga by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
natudah-hazarduari-school.desc: Natudah Secondary School in Damurhuda upazila was founded by the local zamindar Nafarchandra Pal Chowdhury at the request of his wife, and first carried her name as the Radharani Institution. Its 1906 building was laid out by a Kolkata firm on a plan of 15 rooms per floor ringed by corridors, roughly 250 doors to a floor and about a thousand in all, which is why people call it Hazarduari. Only one storey was built on the four-storey foundation. Calcutta University recognised the school in 1909 and it still teaches on a 9-acre campus.
blocks: How to get there
From Chuadanga town go by bus or CNG to Damurhuda and on to Natudah; it fits with a visit to Aat Kobor nearby.
Good to know
It is a working school, so visit on a holiday or after classes and ask at the office before walking around.
